args.note: Bounded: capitalize name's first letter in greet() (hello.py). Existing test_greet asserts lowercase 'hello zharn', which the brief's own example contradicts once greet() capitalizes -- will update that assertion to 'hello Zharn' and add a new test for a second case (e.g. an already-capitalized name) so the suite stays green and covers the new behavior.

args.body:
What changed: hello.py greet() now capitalizes the first letter of name (`f"hello {name[:1].upper()}{name[1:]}"`). test_hello.py's existing test_greet updated to expect "hello Zharn" for greet("zharn") (was asserting the pre-change lowercase behaviour, which the brief's own example contradicts); added test_greet_already_capitalized covering greet("Zharn") == "hello Zharn".

How verified: `python3 -m pytest test_hello.py -q` — before the fix: "1 failed, 1 passed" (test_greet failed with 'hello zharn' != 'hello Zharn'); after the fix: "2 passed in 0.00s".

Where to look first: hello.py:5 (the one-line capitalize fix) and test_hello.py (both assertions).
